topPRs.title: feat(proxyd): consensus_out_of_range_wait for blocks just above consensus
topPRs.author: zhwrd
topPRs.body:
## Problem

In consensus mode, websocket subscriptions and HTTP requests see different heads:

- **WS:** `ProxyWS` connects the client to a single backend, so `newHeads` for block N fires as soon as that backend imports N.
- **HTTP:** `eth_getBlockByNumber(N)` is checked against the consensus latest block. That is the lowest head across the consensus group, refreshed every `consensus_poller_interval`, plus up to one HA heartbeat when `consensus_ha` is on. While N is above it, proxyd answers `null` itself (#552, #769), and state reads get `-32001`.

On a 1s-block chain, a client that fetches each block right after its `newHeads` notification loses this race on nearly every block. One example is Blockscout's realtime fetcher, which turns the `null` into `404 Not Found`, doesn't retry, and leaves the block to its catch-up indexer. We saw about one error per block and blocks reaching the explorer ~45s late.

## Change

New backend group option `consensus_out_of_range_wait`, default `0` (off). When set:

- A request that names a block above the consensus latest block, by at most `consensus_max_block_lag`, waits until consensus reaches that block or the wait elapses.
- It then goes through the normal rewrite path. Responses still come only from consensus backends, and a block that never reaches consensus is still answered as out of range.
- Backends are chosen after the wait. Consensus can advance during it by dropping a lagging backend, and that backend must not then serve the request.
- One HTTP request waits at most `consensus_out_of_range_wait` in total. That includes a batch, which is forwarded as several minibatches (`max_upstream_batch_size`, duplicate-ID groups). A request whose budget is already spent gets outcome `exhausted`. WS messages are forwarded once, so each may wait in full.
- Startup rejects a wait that is not shorter than the server timeout (`timeout_seconds`, default 10s).
- Blocks further ahead than `consensus_max_block_lag` can't be on any consensus backend yet, so they are answered immediately as today.
- CL consensus groups are unaffected.

Supporting changes:

- **Out-of-range error:** the rewrite error is now `*BlockOutOfRangeError{Block}`. It matches `ErrRewriteBlockOutOfRange` via `errors.Is`, so existing checks are unchanged.
- **Wait loop:** it rechecks the in-memory consensus state every 20ms and stops on timeout or when the client cancels.
- **Log ranges:** the block scan probes past the first out-of-range block, so a log range with both ends above the head waits for `toBlock`.
- **New counter:** `proxyd_group_consensus_out_of_range_waits_total{backend_group_name,outcome}` with outcomes `caught_up`, `timeout`, `too_far`, `canceled` and `exhausted`.

Waiting was chosen over routing the request to whichever backend is ahead for three reasons:

1. Consistency guarantees stay the same.
2. It covers every method the rewriter handles, `eth_getLogs`/`eth_newFilter` ranges included.
3. Routing ahead would need method-specific retry-on-missing logic and would still race the poller's per-backend head, which can be up to one poll interval old.

**Trade-offs:**
- A held HTTP request does not take a `max_concurrent_rpcs` slot, since that semaphore is only taken around the backend call. It does hold its connection and goroutine for up to the wait.
- Over WS, a held message keeps its `max_concurrent_ws_rpcs` slot.
- Server drain can take up to one wait longer.

**Not covered:** `eth_getBlockByHash` with the hash from `newHeads`, since proxyd can't place a hash relative to the head.

## Testing

- `integration_tests/consensus_out_of_range_wait_test.go` (new config `consensus_out_of_range_wait.toml`) covers:
  - the block is served once consensus advances mid-wait
  - `null` after the wait if consensus doesn't advance, without hitting the backend
  - no wait beyond `consensus_max_block_lag`
  - no delay for in-range requests
  - a batch whose elements are forwarded as separate minibatches (`max_upstream_batch_size = 1`) serves every element once consensus reaches its blocks
  - three minibatches spend one wait in total
- Unit tests for `highestOutOfRangeBlock`: it finds the max across methods and ranges (both ends of a log range above the head included) and leaves request params untouched.
- `TestStartRejectsOutOfRangeWaitAtServerTimeout` checks the startup check, with an explicit and with the default server timeout. Further unit tests cover `BlockOutOfRangeError` (`errors.Is`/`errors.As`).
- Not covered: a group of more than one backend in which consensus advances by dropping a lagging backend mid-wait.
- Test run: `go test ./...`, `go test -race` on the new test, and `golangci-lint run` (v2.11.4) all pass.

topPRs.title: ci: build images with the unified build-images workflow
topPRs.author: falcorocks
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Build all container images from one v2 catalog, `.github/images.json`, with the reusable `build-images.yaml` workflow in `ethereum-optimism/factory` pinned to `8d8e180e5993952ca1c7e6c6380dc4b2ba7d1bfa`.

- Replaces the docker caller (`build-images.yaml`) and the apko caller (`build-images.apko.yaml`) with the generic caller from the factory template. The apko caller and `.github/images.apko.json` are removed. The docker and apko catalogs are merged into `.github/images.json`, keyed by image name.
- Docker images keep their context and Dockerfile. The apko-built images keep their melange packages, apko configs, and smoke commands. Images built by both builders keep docker as the primary builder, and the apko builder keeps its `apko-` tag prefix.
- Image names and tags are unchanged for the scheduled run (full catalog), for manual runs, and for release tags. Release tags keep the `${version}` publish formula (for example `v4.36.0`) and the `VERSION` build argument. Verified by running the legacy planners and the new planner side by side for the full catalog and for release tags of a dual-builder image, a second dual-builder image, and an apko-only image.
- Accepted extra tag: none.
- The unused `apko_images` key is removed from `images.json`.

Behaviour changes:

- A push to `main` publishes new sha and branch tags only for images whose paths changed. Images not touched by the push keep their previous tags until the daily run, which publishes the full catalog.
- Pull request builds no longer push images. They build `amd64` only, with no registry login and no OIDC token. Publishing runs only on trusted runs (default branch, scheduled, manual, and tags).
- The `pull_request` trigger no longer filters by branch. A `merge_group` trigger is added. The daily schedule (03:00 UTC) and the `*/v*` and `v*` release tag triggers are kept.
- Required check names change because the job names now come from the caller and the reusable workflow. The `result` job of the caller is the single status check to require.
- Publishing runs in the `release` GitHub environment, which exists on this repository for the `main` branch and the `*/v*` and `v*` tags.
- Smoke tests run only for the apko builds, as before. Docker builds have no smoke tests, as before.

Other workflows: none changed. No other workflow in this repository writes to a registry or authenticates to a cloud provider.

topPRs.title: fix(proxyd): accept a group-wide CL rewind instead of emptying the consensus group
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
In consensus-layer mode, proxyd excludes a backend whose finalized or local_safe block is below the group consensus, so that one restarting backend cannot drag consensus backward. Interop supernodes move back together after an invalidation replaces a local-safe block, so every backend was excluded at once. The consensus group became empty, every request except the cached `optimism_syncStatus` failed with "no backend is currently healthy to serve traffic", and it stayed that way until all of them climbed back above the old consensus. This was observed on a two-chain interop devnet with three supernodes behind proxyd-cl.

When every otherwise-eligible backend is below consensus, proxyd now accepts them as a group-wide rewind. A single lagging backend among healthy peers is still excluded.

Related, and not changed here:
- With the default `safe_block_drift_threshold` and `finalized_block_drift_threshold` of 0, any regression of safe or finalized bans a backend for the ban period. The same devnet banned all three supernodes when cross-safe moved back by one block after an invalidation. Supernode backends need non-zero drift thresholds in their proxyd-cl config.
- The supernodes' finalized head was also falling back to the interop anchor after each invalidation, which triggered the finalized-below-consensus exclusion. That is fixed in op-supernode by ethereum-optimism/optimism#24299.

topPRs.title: fix(proxyd): relay WebSocket requests as decoded
topPRs.author: Qumeric
topPRs.body:
The WebSocket path checks the method of the decoded request against `ws_method_whitelist`, then relays the client's original bytes. `encoding/json` matches keys case-insensitively and keeps the last duplicate, so `{"method":"eth_chainId","METHOD":"eth_subscribe"}` passes the whitelist as `eth_subscribe` while a backend that reads the exact `method` key runs `eth_chainId`. That bypasses the whitelist and the limits tied to it.

This relays the request as decoded, as the HTTP path does. Fields the client omitted stay omitted, so notifications stay notifications.
